system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation: elastic restoring force vs. shock-induced inertial force (F = ma). The comb fingers must withstand 10000g without contact. Assuming a proof mass of 1 μg, the inertial force is 10 μN. The restoring force of the suspension must exceed this at maximum deflection. If finger gap is 2 μm, maximum allowable deflection is 1 μm to prevent contact. Current suspension stiffness must be >10 N/m to satisfy this.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — off-the-shelf: increase finger gap from 2 μm to 4 μm (USER CONSTRAINT: requires larger die area), apply hydrophobic coating (e.g., Cytop) to reduce adhesion forces (ASSUMPTION: coating application is feasible at MEMS scale), implement interdigitated finger stoppers with 1 μm gap (CALCULATED: prevents overtravel beyond safe deflection). Procedure: redesign mask layouts, adjust etch processes, integrate coating step in fabrication, verify stop placement via SEM.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — standard practice uses smaller gaps for higher sensitivity, requiring more complex shock protection structures. This approach increases die area by ~50% (USER CONSTRAINT: larger die) but eliminates need for external shock mounts. Maintenance parity with standard devices; cost class increases moderately due to larger die and coating process. Worth it for applications requiring high shock survival without performance degradation.

EXECUTABLE TEST — protocol: mount device on shaker table, apply 10000g half-sine pulse (1 ms duration) in all three axes sequentially, measure zero-g offset before and after each shock using calibrated reference accelerometer. Instruments: shock shaker system, high-speed camera (10,000 fps) to observe finger motion during shock, precision position measurement system. Pass/fail threshold: zero-g offset change <50 mg after all shocks. Duration: 30 minutes including setup and measurement.
